correctness.rationale: All real two-cycles are reduced bijectively to one positive scalar amplitude root. Strict global logarithmic concavity of the amplitude curve for 1<B<=4/3 proves exact root multiplicity and nondegenerate fold. Explicit matrix products yield trace, determinant and the unit-multiplier test; elementary inequalities prove saddle and Schur-stable sink throughout 1<B<=9/8. The 3/2-onset expansion follows from a nondegenerate interior maximum. A standard-library verifier passed 2,526 finite tests; infinite conclusions rest on these proofs.

value.rationale: The absence of fixed points is a defining motivation for the source model, making the existence and stability of its first possible nontrivial periodic orbit a natural dynamical question. The result proves a complete two-versus-one-versus-zero orbit count across a positive gain–forcing region, a genuine sink/saddle coexistence wedge and the sharp nonanalytic 3/2 fold-opening law; none follows from a single numerical plot or a textbook local linearization. No claim of general global chaos or optimal gain cutoff is made.
